_schema.expected_answer: Human-readable reference answer (wording is NOT compared).
_schema.must_contain: EXACT facts that must appear in the answer (case-insensitive substring): amounts, dates, rule names.
_schema.must_not_contain: Strings whose presence means the system fell for the trap (e.g. a stale rate or uncapped fee).
_schema.answer_starts_with: Optional exact opening for yes/no questions.
_schema.expected_citations: EXACT (document, clause) pairs that must be among the cited sources. Extra real citations are allowed.
_schema.adversarial: true if designed to make a naive system fail; 'trap' says how.

cases.question: When does a small merchant receive UPI money?
cases.expected_answer: T+1 (next working day) by default; T+0 same day by 11:59 PM if the merchant has an active Instant Settlement add-on. Circular item A replaced master 1.1 from 01 Aug 2026; merchant size is irrelevant.

cases.question: A large merchant (above Rs.10 lakh monthly) receives a Rs.4,000 UPI payment. What MDR and GST do they pay?
cases.expected_answer: MDR 0.50% x 4,000 = Rs.20.00 (below the Rs.25 cap from circular C; the master's Rs.15 cap is superseded). GST 18% x 20 = Rs.3.60. Total Rs.23.60.

cases.trap: Above the Rs.1,00,000 per-transaction limit; naive system computes uncapped 0.50% = Rs.750 or uses stale Rs.15 cap.
cases.question: A large merchant (above Rs.10 lakh monthly) receives a Rs.1,50,000 UPI payment. What do they pay?
cases.expected_answer: Flag first that Rs.1,50,000 exceeds the Rs.1,00,000 per-transaction UPI limit (4.1) unless the merchant is Capital Markets/Insurance with enhanced KYC (4.2/4.4), and even then the Rs.1,00,000 per-customer daily limit (4.3) conflicts. If processed: MDR capped at Rs.25 (circular C), GST Rs.4.50, total Rs.29.50.

cases.question: A merchant refunds a customer 3 hours after the sale. Do they get the MDR back?
cases.expected_answer: Yes. Clause 3.3 (refund within 24 hours -> MDR reversed in full) is still in force; circular item D only deletes it from 01 Sep 2026.

cases.trap: FAQ and master 3.3 still say 'yes'; circular item D (effective 01 Sep, not the circular's default 01 Aug) deleted 3.3.
cases.question: A merchant refunds a customer 3 hours after the sale. Do they get the MDR back?
cases.expected_answer: No. Clause 3.3 was deleted by circular item D effective 01 Sep 2026; clause 3.2 applies without exception, so MDR is not returned.

cases.trap: Stale FAQ: claims no fee cap.
cases.question: What does the FAQ say about the MDR cap, and is the FAQ right?
cases.expected_answer: FAQ says there is no upper limit. Wrong: master 2.3 capped MDR at Rs.15 from 01 Jan 2026 (before the FAQ was written); from 01 Aug 2026 circular C sets Rs.15 (<= Rs.10 lakh) and Rs.25 (> Rs.10 lakh). FAQ's 0.30% small rate is also stale (0.25%).

cases.question: Can a customer pay Rs.1,00,000 twice in one day to a merchant?
cases.expected_answer: No. Each payment is within the Rs.1,00,000 per-transaction limit, but the Rs.2,00,000 total exceeds the Rs.1,00,000 per-customer daily limit (4.3, as amended by E).

cases.question: I closed my account yesterday. When will I get my money?
cases.expected_answer: Within 10 working days of closure (14 Aug 2026), net of outstanding dues: by 26 Aug 2026 counting only Sundays as non-working (later if bank holidays fall in between). FAQ's '10 days' is wrong; master 5.2 prevails.

cases.question: Does the policy allow me to settle card payments same day?
cases.expected_answer: No. Cards settle T+2 (1.2). The T+0 Instant Settlement option (circular A) is UPI-only.

cases.trap: Amendment not yet effective: on 15 Jul 2026 the circular is issued-soon but not in force, so the Rs.15 cap binds.
cases.question: A large merchant (above Rs.10 lakh monthly) receives a Rs.4,000 UPI payment. What MDR and GST do they pay?
cases.expected_answer: 0.50% x 4,000 = Rs.20 capped at Rs.15 (master 2.3); GST Rs.2.70; total Rs.17.70. FAQ's 'no upper limit' would give Rs.20 and is rejected.

cases.trap: Stale FAQ rate (0.30%) and no cap would give Rs.30; new 0.25% rate uncapped gives Rs.25; correct is the Rs.15 small-merchant cap.
cases.question: A small merchant receives a Rs.10,000 UPI payment. What is the MDR and GST?
cases.expected_answer: 0.25% x 10,000 = Rs.25, capped at Rs.15 (circular C, small tier); GST Rs.2.70; total Rs.17.70.

cases.trap: Boundary: 'up to Rs.10 lakh' is inclusive, so exactly Rs.10 lakh is the small tier.
cases.question: A merchant with monthly volume of exactly Rs.10 lakh receives a Rs.8,000 UPI payment. What MDR do they pay?
cases.expected_answer: Small tier: 0.25% x 8,000 = Rs.20, capped at Rs.15; GST Rs.2.70; total Rs.17.70. (Large tier would wrongly give Rs.25 cap -> Rs.25.)

cases.trap: Missing information: no card MDR exists in any document; a naive system reuses the UPI rate.
cases.question: What is the MDR on a Rs.5,000 card payment?
cases.expected_answer: Cannot answer: the documents only define MDR for UPI.

cases.trap: Cross-reference to a document that was not supplied (Annexure C).
cases.question: What does Annexure C require for enhanced KYC?
cases.expected_answer: Cannot answer: clause 4.4 refers to Annexure C but it is not in the supplied documents.

cases.trap: False premise (there IS a cap); naive system computes 0.50% x 90,000 = Rs.450.
cases.question: Since there is no upper limit on MDR, how much MDR and GST does a large merchant pay on a Rs.90,000 UPI payment?
cases.expected_answer: The premise is wrong: MDR is capped. 0.50% x 90,000 = Rs.450, capped at Rs.25; GST Rs.4.50; total Rs.29.50.

cases.trap: Question quotes a deleted clause as if it were in force.
cases.question: Under clause 3.3, refunds within 24 hours get the MDR reversed. A merchant refunds 2 hours after the sale. How much MDR is reversed?
cases.expected_answer: None. Clause 3.3 was deleted by circular item D from 01 Sep 2026; MDR is not returned (3.2).

cases.trap: Date before any policy document is in force.
cases.question: When does a merchant get UPI settlement?
cases.expected_answer: Cannot answer: the Master Document only takes effect on 01 Jan 2026.

cases.trap: Topic keyword ('chargeback') present, but the asked-for concept (penalty) is not in the documents.
cases.question: What is the penalty for a late chargeback?
cases.expected_answer: Cannot answer: no penalty is mentioned anywhere.

cases.question: How many days does the customer's bank have to raise a chargeback?
cases.expected_answer: 120 days (clause 3.4).

cases.trap: Amended clause (circular E): the customer's lower bank limit now applies; master alone would allow it.
cases.question: The customer's bank limit is Rs.50,000 per day. Can they pay Rs.60,000 to my shop in one UPI payment?
cases.expected_answer: No. Since 01 Aug 2026 the daily limit is the lower of Rs.1,00,000 and the customer's bank limit (Rs.50,000).

cases.trap: Unresolved internal contradiction: 4.2 allows Rs.2,00,000 per transaction, 4.3 caps a customer at Rs.1,00,000 per day; no precedence stated.
cases.question: Can an insurance merchant with enhanced KYC accept Rs.1,50,000 in one UPI payment?
cases.expected_answer: Cannot answer definitively: 4.2/4.4 allow it but the per-customer daily limit in 4.3 blocks it, and no clause sets precedence.

cases.question: Can a merchant refund a customer 100 days after the sale?
cases.expected_answer: No: refunds must be initiated within 90 days (3.1).

cases.question: Can I get my UPI money the same day?
cases.expected_answer: No. Before 01 Aug 2026 UPI settles T+1 for everyone; the T+0 add-on only exists from 01 Aug 2026.

cases.question: A merchant refunds a customer 30 hours after the sale. Do they get the MDR back?
cases.expected_answer: No. More than 24 hours, so 3.2 applies even before 3.3 was deleted.

cases.trap: Sale before and refund after the 01 Sep 2026 deletion of 3.3; the documents do not say which date governs.
cases.question: A customer paid at 11 PM on 31 August 2026 and the merchant refunded 2 hours later on 1 September 2026. Is the MDR returned?
cases.expected_answer: Cannot answer definitively: under the transaction date 3.3 reverses MDR; under the refund date item D deleted 3.3 and 3.2 applies. No transition rule is given.
